subject: Request: Stability & Activation Bridge for Vanguard Enterprise Deal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: Stability & Activation Bridge for Vanguard Enterprise Deal

Team —

Quick context: Vanguard has signaled a conditional go/no-go for pilot activation at the end of Q2 (target internal kick-off 2028-05-15). Procurement needs the SOW and a mapped activation path before 2028-04-20. They flagged two gating concerns in the technical review:

1) Stability under long-tail sequence variance — they expect multi-minute sessions with mixed short/long prompts.
2) Deterministic fallback behavior and an "activation bridge" plan (how we degrade gracefully if a dedicated pool saturates).

I've attached a one-page customer MAP and the current SOW draft (SOW_draft_vanguard.docx). Request: Can Eng + Product provide a scoped stability gate and activation-bridge implementation plan we can commit to in the SOW? Specifically we need:

- Short answer on feasibility for Canary path + fallback model variant (yes/no + approx dev effort in engineer-weeks).
- Minimum telemetry hooks and trace IDs we must add to satisfy Vanguard's audit team.
- A timeboxed plan for a low-risk canary (3 checkpoints: smoke, perf, rollback).

Constraints/asks from Sales: we need this scoped and a one-page summary by 2028-04-12 to include in procurement and to avoid losing the activation date. Vendor notes in the MAP (vanguard_mmap_v1.pdf).

Thanks — I know this is tight. Happy to join a quick 30m sync today or tomorrow.

Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vanguard_mmap_v1.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: SOW_draft_vanguard.docx (draft)

Subject: Re: Request: Stability & Activation Bridge for Vanguard Enterprise Deal

Irene —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. High-level response after a quick scan:

- Canary + fallback: Feasible. We already have most of the runtime primitives (model variants, routing policies, prefix caching) but we need two engineering pieces to make this production-safe:
  1) A deterministic fallback router that promotes a compatible lower-capacity variant when the primary pool is above threshold (ETA: 2.5 engineer-weeks to implement + 1 week for testing).
  2) Minor telemetry extension to capture session-level sequence-length histograms and cross-request trace propagation (ETA: 1.0 engineer-week).

- Risk: The main unknown is the compatibility of their prompt mix with quantized model variants — we should plan an eval sweep on their canonical prompt set. That’s product/ML ops work more than infra.

Proposed minimal canary checkpoints:
  A. Smoke: single-region canary with 5% traffic and SLOs verified for 24h.
  B. Perf: 48h run at expected QPS with latency/99s monitored.
  C. Rollback: Automated rollback policy if error-rate > 2% or tail latency regression > 30%.

I'll carve out time for a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00-10:30 to align scope unless you prefer a different slot. CCing Marissa for product tradeoffs and Karthik for infra scheduling.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

All —

Appreciate the quick reply, Jonas. A couple of points from Sales/Customer side to help prioritize:

- Procurement timeline is firm: they must include the SOW and activation commitment in the vendor packet by EOD 2028-04-20. If we can't commit to a bounded effort in the SOW, procurement will push for longer evaluation windows which will kill our Q2 kickoff.
- They asked specifically for a mitigation commitment: "If activation triggers capacity saturation, Redwood will provide an activation bridge with documented rollback steps and 24/7 escalation contact for the first 72 hours." We can scope that operationally (on-call + runbook) rather than as code, but the detection hooks must be automated.

Proposal (to product/eng):
  1) Commit to a scoped implementation of the deterministic fallback router with the testing cadence Jonas suggested (2.5 + 1 weeks dev/test).
  2) Product to own the eval sweep against their prompt set (Marissa). If that fails, we will document expected regressions and propose a conservative initial model variant.
  3) CS to assemble the operational runbook and escalation roster (Sean/Irene) for the 72h activation window.

If product/eng can get me a one-page commitment (feasibility, effort, rollback conditions, telemetry required) by 2028-04-12, I will push procurement to accept that in the SOW and lock the 05-15 kickoff.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

Thanks — updated plan below. I pulled in product and ML ops scope and made tradeoffs explicit so Sales/procurement can include a clean commitment in the SOW.

Summary (one-page commitment for procurement):
- Feasibility: Canary + deterministic fallback: YES. Dependencies: engineering router change + eval sweep on their prompt set.
- Effort estimate (Rough): Eng router ~2.5 engineer-weeks, end-to-end test + canary orchestration ~1 week, telemetry + trace propagation ~1 engineer-week, eval sweep (product/ML ops) ~1.5 engineer-weeks. Total cross-team effort ~6 engineer-weeks (split across teams).
- Rollback conditions (we will commit these in SOW):
  • Error-rate >2% (5m rolling) OR
  • 99th percentile latency regression >30% (observed for >30m) OR
  • Any functional regression on the seed prompt set with severity >P2.
- Telemetry: session ID propagation, sequence-length histograms, request model-variant tag, trace ID linking to Walkthroughs. Minimal dashboard + alerting for 24/7 on-call.
- Operational bridge: CS will provide a 72-hour escalation roster and runbook; Product will own rollback decision criteria.
- Delivered artifacts by 2028-04-12: one-page commitment, technical appendix (short bulleted list of infra changes), SOW language snippet.

Tradeoffs/notes:
- If the eval sweep shows >10% degradation on quantized variant, we recommend either a short-term pruning of quantization for that customer or an expanded canary window. That is a commercial tradeoff (cost vs. accuracy).
- We will not commit to full automation of fallback within the initial SOW release; the first release includes an operator-assisted automated rollback (manual approval for final shift).

Irene/Sean — if that meets your needs I will draft the one-pager today and share the SOW snippet for procurement. Jonas/Karthik — please confirm the eng estimates so I can finalize.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
